title: Enterprise Request Curation: Adaptive Onboarding & Proof-of-Need Workflow for Hosted Streaming + Toolchains
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers keep submitting high-effort feature asks for hosted chat streaming + tool/function-calling with incomplete signal (no production prompt sets, missing SLA constraints, unclear integration topology). Current intake is manual, slow, and inconsistent across triage leads which causes long decision latency and missed early-signal pilots.

Goal: Build an adaptive onboarding and Proof-of-Need (PoN) workflow that standardizes signal capture, scores requests against enterprise criteria, and produces a deterministic decision within 72 hours for typical cases. The flow should make it easy for customers to supply reproducible prompts and example structured-output schemas, and for product/eng to run a short pilot to validate cost/latency/regression risk before full prioritization.

Proposed solution summary:
1) Intake form evolution: require minimal reproducible artifact (sample prompt set, expected structured schema, expected throughput, acceptable tail latency, compliance notes). Provide a guided checklist and optional telemetry connector for customers on Dedicated or Private to share anonymized traces.
2) Scoring engine: implement an automated weighted rubric combining: SLA urgency (0.35), revenue/strategic value (0.25), security/regulatory risk (0.15), engineering complexity (0.15), and early-validation feasibility (0.10). Each factor maps to discrete signals (e.g., paying seat count, token/sec estimate, existing integration maturity).
3) PoN pilot path: for requests with score in the "Pilot" band, run a 2-week sandbox pilot (small reserved capacity or simulated load) with three artifacts: sample prompts, evaluation metrics (latency, cost per 1k tokens, regression A/B on canonical prompts), and a short TOC decision doc.
4) Onboarding Concierge: assign a product-solution owner for high-touch customers to complete the intake and coordinate PoN. Provide templates and a Slack command to pull the triage score and recommended next step.
5) Observability hooks: capture telemetry (prefix cache hit rate, KV cache warmup time, streaming error rate, fallback-to-slower-model rate) during pilot and expose a dashboard template for the customer and triage reviewers.

Why this is different: rather than a free-form backlog, this creates a reproducible funnel that reduces review friction, surfaces engineering cost early, and protects SLAs by explicitly validating streaming + tool calls. The PoN path gives us data to make better prioritization decisions and shortens time-to-value for customers.

Out-of-scope: full automation of customer billing changes, Dedicated capacity provisioning flows (this ticket integrates via dependencies), and on-prem install orchestration.
acceptance_criteria: A web intake form is live with mandatory fields: sample prompt set (min 10 prompts), expected TPS and acceptable p95 latency, intended structured-output spec (JSON schema), security/regulatory notes, and customer business signal.
A scoring engine prototype exists (endpoint + simple UI) that calculates a deterministic score and band (Decline|Backlog|Pilot|Fast-track) based on the weighted rubric.
Pilot runbook and a dashboard template (latency, cost/1k tokens, prefix cache hit, fallback rate, error rate) are published and linked in the ticket.
Pilot path executed for at least 2 pilot requests from different customers and triage decision taken within 72 hours for non-blocking cases.
Triage owners and Onboarding Concierge assignment workflow documented; Slack command /triage-score returns a link to the intake and recommended next step.
Telemetry contract for pilot captured and a stub telemetry connector available for Dedicated customers to share anonymized traces.
Documentation and internal playbook written and approved by PM, Design, and Eng; 2 demos run with sales/solutions engineering team.
Rollout plan exists and no critical unresolved security flags (security_review_required = false as per preliminary assessment).
success_metrics: Median time-to-decision for enterprise feature requests reduced from 9 business days to <=72 hours for non-blocking cases
Fraction of intake requests that have complete reproducible artifacts increased from ~22% to >=80%
Pilot-to-implementation conversion rate measured (target initial benchmark >=30%)
Average triage reviewer time per request reduced by 40%
Early pilot telemetry provides actionable insights in >=90% of pilots (dashboard populated with >3 metrics).
